meta.title: StockBot data picture guide
meta.subtitle: What is in the database, which table holds what, where it comes from, and how it reaches the engine.
meta.banner: The lake (finsight.db) is read-only for the engine.
meta.example_note: Everything labelled EXAMPLE is made up. Numbers without that label are measured or quoted from a named report, with their date.

groups.label: Core price data
groups.desc: Daily raw prices. The one table the engine reads for prices.

groups.label: Corporate actions
groups.desc: Splits, bonuses and other events by ex-date, and the symbol-rename map.

groups.label: Earnings
groups.desc: Board-meeting and results announcements from the NSE earnings APIs.

groups.label: ASM / GSM
groups.desc: NSE surveillance lists, one snapshot per day.

groups.label: Shares and listings
groups.desc: Shares issued today and NSE's list of listed securities.

groups.label: Staging and logs
groups.desc: Where data landed first, what was archived, and diaries of the downloaders.

groups.label: Legacy dashboard
groups.desc: Used only by the older dashboard side, not connected to the new engine.

groups.label: Empty or unused
groups.desc: No rows, no reader, or SQLite's own bookkeeping.

databases.name: finsight.db
databases.writers: The ingestion tools, the one-off tools in scripts/provenance, and the older dashboard side.
databases.readers: AsOfView (read-only), the data checks, the live runner (ASM/GSM snapshot), tests.
databases.engine_may: Read-only, only through open_lake (SQLite mode=ro plus query_only). The engine, backtest, validation and the live adapter never write it.
databases.plain: The one big database of prices, corporate actions, earnings and surveillance lists. Everything the engine knows about the market comes from here.
databases.when: size measured {{m:meta.measured_date}}; roles from DATA_GUIDE section A

databases.name: state/live_state.db
databases.writers: stockbot/live/state_store.py, through the live adapter only.
databases.engine_may: Not directly. The engine only sees the State object the adapter loads. The store refuses to open a file named finsight.db.
databases.plain: The live account's own database: an append-only journal of everything that happened, plus a cached copy of the latest state. Created by the first end-of-day run.
databases.when: checked 2026-11-09: the end-of-day run has never been run

databases.name: asm_gsm_snapshot.db
databases.writers: The frozen stand-alone script snapshot_asm_gsm.py in that same folder.
databases.readers: stockbot/data/ingestion/merge_asm_gsm_snapshots.py, when you choose to merge it into the lake.
databases.engine_may: No. It holds one snapshot day, 2026-11-08.
databases.plain: A separate small database where the daily ASM/GSM snapshot tool saves its pages. It has the same three snapshot tables as the lake.

databases.name: data/reference/
databases.writers: The scripts named in the Other databases view.
databases.readers: Some are read by the as-of view (fund_etf_symbols.csv) and the sector lookup (sector_map.csv); the rest by checks and tools.
databases.engine_may: Some files, through named readers. Never written by the engine.
databases.plain: Lookup and evidence files that live in git next to the code: sectors, fund lists, the ISIN map, the raw corporate-action dump and the 57 verified events.
databases.when: file count measured {{m:meta.measured_date}}; 57 verified events from DATA_GUIDE section E

databases.name: Trial ledgers
databases.engine_may: No. Never edited. The exploratory ledger is pinned by a recorded sha256 and has no hash chain.
databases.plain: The record of every validation attempt, counted whether it passed or not. It is the honesty record for the validation step.

databases.name: state/tickets/
databases.plain: One file per trading day listing the tickets the engine proposed. Not written yet, because the end-of-day run has never run.

databases.name: Backups
databases.size: three lake copies, each with a .sha256 file
databases.writers: Made by hand before risky steps.
databases.plain: Hand-made copies of the lake from before the three risky steps. The newest, pre_restructure, has the same sha256 as today's finsight.db.

heads_up.text: No daily loader exists yet. Nothing moves new days from staging into the lake.
ASM/GSM history exists only from the day snapshots began: {{m:coverage.asm_days.0.snapshot_date}}. Snapshot days so far: {{m:coverage.asm_days|uniq:snapshot_date}}.
The trading calendar starts {{m:coverage.nifty_first_date}}. Earlier lake dates cannot be reached for decisions.
Prices are raw, never split-adjusted. Only the EQ series was kept.
{{m:coverage.actions_after_last_session|n}} corporate actions already have an ex-date after the lake's last session.

tables.oneline: Daily raw prices for every symbol, plus the Nifty 50 and India VIX series.
tables.purpose: One row per symbol per session: raw open, high, low, close and volume, exactly as traded. Never adjusted for splits. Everything the engine knows about prices comes from here through AsOfView.

columns.symbol: NSE symbol. A renamed name is stored under its latest symbol for the whole history.
columns.open_raw: Opening price in rupees as traded that day.
columns.high_raw: Highest price of the day, raw.
columns.low_raw: Lowest price of the day, raw.
columns.close_raw: Closing price, raw. A split shows as a jump here.
columns.volume_raw: Shares traded. Zero for the index series.
columns.source: Provenance label, set on some index rows only. Not reliable provenance.
columns.loaded_at: Load time of the F2 work. Empty on most rows.
columns.source_symbol: The symbol the row was published under, when it differs from symbol (renamed names).

issues: EQ series only: a name that leaves EQ looks like a long absence.
Raw prices: a split shows as a jump.
The Nifty series starts later than the equity rows.

tables.oneline: The raw Bhavcopy download as it landed, before it went into the lake.
tables.purpose: Raw end-of-day rows with the extra Bhavcopy fields: ISIN, previous close, series. It is the evidence behind the lake and the input for symbol continuity. Only EQ rows were kept.

columns.prev_close: Previous close as printed in the file, an independent corporate-action signal.
columns.series: NSE series. Only EQ was kept.

issues: Ends on the last date requested; nothing moves new days from staging into the lake automatically.

tables.oneline: The old Yahoo-adjusted lake rows, archived when the swap replaced them.
tables.purpose: The lake as it was before the F2 swap: Yahoo-adjusted prices with fractional values. Kept as evidence. Nothing in the engine reads it.

columns.open_raw: Named raw, but holds a Yahoo-ADJUSTED value.
columns.created_at: When the Yahoo data was loaded.
columns.archived_at: When the swap archived the row.

issues: The column names say _raw but the content is adjusted: do not use it as raw price evidence.

tables.oneline: A diary of the downloader: one row per calendar date tried.
tables.purpose: Records for each date tried whether it was a session, a holiday or an error. Lets the downloader resume and shows which weekdays were holidays.

columns.status: OK or HOLIDAY_OR_MISSING. An ERROR status exists in the code but none is stored now.
columns.n_rows: EQ rows stored for the date. Zero if not a session.
columns.url: File URL used. Empty for holidays.

issues: NSE answers some holiday requests with the previous session's file; the downloader rejects a file whose own date differs.

tables.oneline: Nifty 50 and India VIX rows for dates the lake lacked.
tables.purpose: Index rows for special weekend sessions and a few ordinary days, fetched from NSE's daily index file or from Yahoo. Applied into the lake by the swap script.

columns.source: An NSE index-file URL or yahoo:<ticker>.

tables.oneline: Every corporate action by ex-date, with an evidence tier.
tables.purpose: One row per symbol, ex-date and type: splits, bonuses, dividends, rights, mergers, demergers and others, with the ratio where one applies. This table makes adjusted prices possible.

columns.symbol: Lake symbol the event applies to.
columns.action_type: SPLIT, BONUS, DIVIDEND, RIGHTS, MERGER, DEMERGER or OTHER.
columns.ratio_numerator: Ratio numerator, for SPLIT, BONUS and RIGHTS.
columns.notes: The feed's subject text and feed symbol.
columns.evidence_tier: STRONG, WEAK, WEAK_DIRECTIONAL, UNSUPPORTED or NOT_PRICE_MOVING.
columns.evidence: The evidence sentence for SPLIT and BONUS rows.

issues: Only the ex-date is recorded, no announcement date.
created_at says nothing about when an event was known: the table was loaded in one go.

tables.oneline: Which symbol an ISIN traded under, and when.
tables.purpose: A map from ISIN, the permanent security identifier, to the symbols it used and the dates, so a rename can be told from a genuinely new security.

columns.first_date: First Bhavcopy day under that symbol.
columns.last_date: Last Bhavcopy day under that symbol.
columns.canonical_symbol: The symbol the history is stored under in the lake.

tables.oneline: One shares-issued number per symbol, as of today, not point-in-time.
tables.purpose: How many shares each company has issued today, fetched once from Yahoo for the market-cap gate. It is not point-in-time, so the engine does not read it.

columns.effective_date: A placeholder date, the same for every row.

issues: KI-001: one current snapshot, not point-in-time, so a market-cap rule cannot be applied to history.

tables.oneline: NSE's list of listed securities with official listing dates.
tables.purpose: Company name, series and listing date for each listed security. Used by tools. The as-of view works out listing age from the first price bar instead.

tables.oneline: Joins a lake symbol to the symbol the earnings APIs use.
tables.purpose: The two symbols differ for renamed names. This map lets the earnings tables be reached from a lake symbol.

columns.query_symbol: Symbol the NSE earnings APIs know it by.
columns.how: lake_symbol means same name; isin_symbol_map means matched through the ISIN map.

tables.oneline: Board-meeting announcements, with the time the exchange was told.
tables.purpose: Every board meeting in the NSE feed with its intimation timestamp. A results meeting counts as known only after its intimation, which makes this the point-in-time-safe source.

columns.is_results_meeting: 1 if classified as a financial-results meeting.
columns.results_rule: Which rule classified it: purpose or desc.
columns.row_hash: Hash of the row, the dedupe key.

issues: A few results meetings have no intimation time and are never returned by the view.

tables.oneline: Filed financial results, used for cross-checks only.
tables.purpose: Filed results with period, audit status and timestamps. Checks use it to cross-check meeting dates. The view does not, because its broadcast time lags the announcement.

columns.broadcast_ts: When it was broadcast. Lags the real announcement.
columns.row_hash: Hash of the row, the dedupe key.

issues: No filings for periods after December 2024 (KI-004).

tables.oneline: The exact API responses, compressed.
tables.purpose: The raw responses so the parsed earnings tables can be rebuilt or audited. A symbol counts as having data if some response returned rows.

tables.oneline: One row per API call of the earnings collection.
tables.purpose: When, which endpoint and symbol, the HTTP status, rows returned and a note.

tables.oneline: NSE's ASM and GSM surveillance lists for the day the snapshot was taken.
tables.purpose: One row per name per framework per day. The live runner excludes any name on today's list. It is point-in-time only from its first day, because the NSE API returns current lists only.

columns.snapshot_date: The day the snapshot was taken. Part of the key.
columns.framework: ASM_LT, ASM_ST or GSM. Part of the key.
columns.symbol: NSE symbol. Part of the key.

issues: KI-003: only snapshot days exist, no history before the first one.

tables.oneline: The raw API body of each ASM or GSM snapshot call.
tables.purpose: Keeps the raw response of each snapshot so the parsed table can be rebuilt.

tables.oneline: Outcome of each snapshot call.
tables.purpose: A missed day shows up as a missing snapshot_date here.

tables.oneline: An older ASM/GSM list design, never filled.
tables.purpose: From the first version of the dashboard side. Its writer has no caller and nothing reads it.

tables.oneline: An older earnings-calendar design, never filled.
tables.purpose: From the first version of the dashboard side. Its writer has no caller, and KI-004 explains why that design could not give a valid calendar.

tables.oneline: The old strategy's daily macro kill-switch state.
tables.purpose: Nifty against its 200- and 50-day averages, the VIX, and a re-entry counter. Used only by the legacy dashboard, not an input of the new engine.

columns.kill_switch_active: 1 means the switch was on, no new entries.
columns.reentry_consecutive_count: Sessions in a row meeting the re-entry condition.

tables.oneline: The old end-of-day pipeline's run diary.
tables.purpose: One row per run of the old pipeline, also its idempotency guard. The new end-of-day run does not use it.

tables.oneline: Open positions of the old paper and live trading. Empty.
tables.purpose: Belongs to the older dashboard side and is not connected to the new state store.

columns.last_partial_exit_rr: Reward to risk of the last partial exit.
columns.next_partial_exit_rr: Reward to risk of the next partial exit.

tables.oneline: Append-only log of closed trades of the old paper and live trading. Empty.
tables.purpose: Two triggers refuse any UPDATE or DELETE. Not connected to the new engine.

columns.excluded_ca: True if an unhandled corporate action excludes the trade from statistics.

tables.oneline: Tickets of each old end-of-day run. Empty.
tables.purpose: The old pipeline's daily candidate list. Its writer was removed.

columns.risk_pct_of_equity: Risk as a share of equity.

tables.oneline: Deposits and withdrawals of the old dashboard. Empty.
tables.purpose: Cash movements for the old equity calculation. Not connected to the new state store.

tables.oneline: SQLite's own bookkeeping: the next id for each autoincrement table.
tables.purpose: Not a data table. Ignore it.

link_keys.symbol: The same NSE symbol in both tables. A logical link: no foreign key enforces it.
link_keys.isin: The same ISIN in both tables. The ISIN survives a rename, so it ties old and new symbols together.
link_keys.trade_date: The same session date in both tables.
link_keys.ex_date: A corporate action's ex-date is compared with the trade dates of the price table. Nothing joins them in the database.
link_keys.query_symbol: The symbol the NSE earnings APIs use. Reached from a lake symbol through earnings_symbol_map.

er_edges.meaning: One fetch-log row per trade_date the downloader tried.
Staging rows were swapped into the lake with the same symbol and trade_date.
The old Yahoo rows the swap replaced were archived under the same symbol and date.
Fills missing NIFTY50_INDEX and INDIA_VIX dates in the lake.
An action's symbol is a lake symbol; its ex_date is compared with the lake's trade dates.
The ISIN map was built from the ISIN printed in the staging rows.
Renamed names reach the earnings APIs under their old symbol, matched through the ISIN map.
A lake symbol is the lake_symbol column of the earnings map.
Meetings are stored under the query symbol.
Filings are stored under the query symbol.
Raw responses are stored per query symbol.
A snapshot symbol is a lake symbol on the day it was listed.
The official listing list shares the symbol, and an ISIN, with the price table.
Shares issued today per symbol. Unused by the engine.

flow_steps.title: Sources
flow_steps.plain: Five public NSE sources. Nothing here is ours.

flow_steps.title: Scripts fetch and save
flow_steps.plain: Each source has its own script that saves a table. The scripts are run by hand.

flow_steps.title: Tables
flow_steps.plain: The fetched data lands in tables. Prices land in staging first.

flow_steps.title: The missing link
flow_steps.plain: Staging reached the lake by one reviewed swap. No daily step moves new days. That is missing.

flow_steps.title: The lake
flow_steps.plain: Prices and index series in market_data_lake are what the engine reads.

flow_steps.title: Read paths
flow_steps.plain: Prices, actions and earnings go through AsOfView. The surveillance list is read by the live runner.

flow_steps.title: Engine
flow_steps.plain: The engine receives plain data. It cannot reach the database itself.

flow_nodes.label: NSE Bhavcopy zip
flow_nodes.detail: The exchange's end-of-day price file for each session, in a legacy and a 2024+ UDiFF format.

flow_nodes.label: ingest_raw_bhavcopy_range.py
flow_nodes.detail: Tries every calendar date, accepts a file only if it declares the requested date and has EQ rows, and logs the outcome.

flow_nodes.label: market_data_lake_staging
flow_nodes.detail: Raw EQ rows with ISIN, previous close and series, plus one fetch-log row per date tried.

flow_nodes.label: daily loader
flow_nodes.detail: No code moves a new day from staging into the lake. The loader that inserts straight into the lake has no caller. Today the lake ends where the older live pipeline stopped.

flow_nodes.label: market_data_lake
flow_nodes.detail: The lake's price table. Filled from staging by the one-time reviewed swap, f2_swap.py.

flow_nodes.label: NSE index file, Yahoo
flow_nodes.detail: NSE's daily index file, with Yahoo as the fallback, for dates the lake's index series lacked.

flow_nodes.label: f2_index_gap_fill.py
flow_nodes.detail: Fetches index rows for the missing dates.

flow_nodes.label: index_gap_fill
flow_nodes.detail: Index rows waiting to be applied. The swap script applied them into the lake once.

flow_nodes.label: NSE corporate actions API
flow_nodes.detail: The exchange's feed of splits, bonuses, dividends and other actions.

flow_nodes.label: dump, evidence, loader
flow_nodes.detail: Dumps the feed, tests each event against what prices did, labels an evidence tier, and loads once, append-only.

flow_nodes.label: corporate_actions_log
flow_nodes.detail: Every action with ex-date, ratio and evidence tier.

flow_nodes.label: NSE results and board-meeting APIs
flow_nodes.detail: The exchange's APIs for board meetings and filed results.

flow_nodes.label: collect_earnings_history.py
flow_nodes.detail: Calls both APIs per symbol, keeps the raw response and the parsed rows.

flow_nodes.label: earnings tables
flow_nodes.detail: Board meetings with intimation time, filings, raw responses and the symbol map.

flow_nodes.label: NSE ASM and GSM lists
flow_nodes.detail: The exchange's surveillance lists. The API returns only today's list, never history.

flow_nodes.label: snapshot_asm_gsm.py
flow_nodes.detail: Saves today's lists. It was run once, on the first snapshot day.

flow_nodes.label: daily scheduler
flow_nodes.detail: No scheduled task runs the snapshot each day on this machine, so a missed day stays missed.

flow_nodes.label: asm_gsm_daily_snapshot
flow_nodes.sub: one row per name per day
flow_nodes.detail: The day's lists, one row per name per framework.

flow_nodes.label: AsOfView prices
flow_nodes.detail: raw_bars, adjusted_bars, sessions, symbols_trading, symbol_info and adtv, all bounded by the as-of date.

flow_nodes.label: AsOfView.corporate_actions
flow_nodes.detail: Returns only actions whose ex-date is on or before the as-of date.

flow_nodes.label: AsOfView earnings
flow_nodes.detail: results_meetings returns a meeting only after its intimation date. No data means no data, not no event.

flow_nodes.label: live.runner.load_asm_ranges
flow_nodes.detail: Reads the day's snapshot and hands the engine plain data. Missing snapshot for the run date stops a live run.

flow_nodes.label: engine.decide + universe
flow_nodes.detail: The engine never opens a database. It receives what the read paths hand it.

row_steps.title: Raw file line
row_steps.plain: NSE publishes one line per security per day in a zip file. The line below is made up.

row_steps.title: Checks
row_steps.plain: Kept only if the file's own date equals the requested date, and only for series EQ. A holiday copy of yesterday's file is rejected.
fields: dropped, and the fetch log says why

row_steps.title: Staging row
row_steps.plain: Names change to the table's own: raw prices, prev_close, isin, series, and the file's URL.

row_steps.title: Fetch log row
row_steps.plain: One diary row for the date: how many EQ rows were stored, with the outcome.

row_steps.title: Into the lake
row_steps.plain: The swap copied raw staging rows into the lake. Prices stay raw. It is a one-time step today: no daily loader exists.

row_steps.title: Freshness check
row_steps.plain: Before a live run the check asks: is today a Nifty date in the lake? If the latest session is older, it stops with DataFreshnessError. It only looks, it never fetches.
fields: fresh: the run may go on

time.error_text: end {later} is after the as-of date {as_of}
lines: AsOfView(conn, as_of) bounds the SQL itself: trade_date <= as_of.
Asking for a later end or start date raises FutureDataError instead of silently returning less.
A split counts only once its ex-date is on or before the as-of date.

SPLIT.price: Factor = numerator / denominator (1:10 gives 0.1). Bars before the ex-date are multiplied.
SPLIT.position: Prices rescaled, shares divided by the factor (floor), cash in lieu for the fraction.

DIVIDEND.price: Ignored: gross returns, no total-return adjustment.

RIGHTS.position: HOLD: flagged CORPORATE_ACTION_HOLD, not rescaled, excluded from trade statistics.

OTHER.price: Factor 1.0. Includes split or bonus announcements whose price evidence disagreed, kept as OTHER on purpose.

actions_text.applies: The engine adjusts prices for SPLIT and BONUS only.
actions_text.means: Any price jump on the date of a dividend, rights issue, merger, demerger or OTHER action stays in the history as an unadjusted jump. A backtest reader should treat it that way.

tiers.STRONG: The Yahoo-implied factor agrees with the logged factor within 3%.
tiers.WEAK: The raw close-to-close ratio is within 25% of the logged factor and closer to it than to any other standard ratio.
tiers.WEAK_DIRECTIONAL: Reviewer-approved: the feed states the ratio, Yahoo does not contradict it, and adjusting improves the fit.
tiers.UNSUPPORTED: The evidence disagreed. Stored as OTHER and does not move prices.
tiers.NOT_PRICE_MOVING: Dividends, rights, mergers, demergers and other non-price events.

issues.title: Shares count is not point-in-time
issues.what: shares_outstanding holds one current number per symbol, fetched once. It cannot say how many shares existed in the past.
issues.backtest: A market-cap rule cannot be applied to history, so the gate is parked and liquidity (ADTV) is used instead.

issues.title: Max-T test has low power
issues.what: At the number of trades the strategy can achieve, the significance test can detect only large edges.
issues.backtest: Not significant at about 2.6 trades a month is not evidence of no edge.

issues.title: No historical ASM/GSM data
issues.what: NSE's API returns the current lists only, so snapshots exist only from the day they began.
issues.backtest: The surveillance exclusion cannot be applied to the past.

issues.title: Earnings history has limits
issues.what: The results API has no filings for periods after December 2024, broadcast times lag the announcement, and some symbols have no data.
issues.backtest: Use the results board-meeting date and its intimation time. No data returns no data, never no event.

issues.title: EQ series only: gaps and re-entries
issues.what: A name that moves out of the EQ series looks like a long absence. {{m:coverage.symbol_class[class=last bar before the last session of the lake].symbols|n}} equity symbols end before the last session.
issues.backtest: Entry and universe rules must treat re-entry after an absence explicitly.

issues.title: Corporate actions have no announcement date
issues.what: Only the ex-date is recorded. The table was loaded in one go, so created_at says nothing about when an event was known.
issues.backtest: No rule may use that an action is coming.

issues.title: Nothing loads new days into the lake
issues.what: The range downloader writes only to staging. The loader that writes straight into the lake has no caller. The lake ends {{m:coverage.lake_last_date}}.
issues.backtest: For the daily run, the freshness check reports DataFreshnessError for any later date until something loads those days.

issues.title: The calendar starts {{m:coverage.nifty_first_date}}
issues.what: Sessions come from the Nifty series. Earlier lake dates have no Nifty row, so they are unreachable for decisions.
issues.backtest: A window that starts earlier effectively starts on that date.

tables.name: meta
tables.plain: schema_version and initial_cash. A different schema version is refused: no migration is designed.

tables.name: journal
tables.plain: The append-only history. kind is init, effect (an operator report applied) or decisions (one session). UNIQUE (kind, key), so the same report or session is journaled once.

tables.name: snapshot
tables.plain: The latest State as JSON. A cache; rebuild ignores it.

events.note: A session's Decisions: a ticket was proposed. No money has moved yet.
The operator reported the fill. apply_effect updates cash and positions (costs left out of this picture).
Next session: the position is stepped, nothing to report.

live.rebuild: rebuild() ignores the snapshot and folds the journal from the first row: init, then each effect with apply_effect, each decisions row with apply_decisions. The result must equal the stored snapshot. scripts/daily_health_check.py reports a mismatch.

ref_files.plain: Sector per symbol, for the sector cap.
ETF and fund names excluded from the universe.
The ISIN map with continuity evidence. The table isin_symbol_map is its loaded form.
Special weekend or holiday sessions and Nifty-series gaps.
The 57 hand-verified events with expected factor and treatment.
Events that move price but are not adjusted (rights, demergers and so on).
Events held out of the first load until a second source confirmed them.
Point-in-time shares inputs of the closed F2b work. Not used.
Point-in-time shares spot-check inputs. Not used.

ref_other.plain: The symbol list used for the corporate-action dump.
The old strategy's random-entry trade library.

ask.q: What did a stock trade at on a day?
ask.plain: Raw prices are stored. The adjusted view is computed in memory from the corporate-action log.

ask.q: Was a day a trading session?
ask.plain: Sessions are the NIFTY50_INDEX dates. The fetch log explains holidays.

ask.q: Did a stock split or pay a bonus, and when?
ask.plain: One row per action with the ex-date and the ratio.

ask.method: actions around the date, then the ISIN map for a rename
ask.plain: Look for an action near the date. If there is none, check whether the symbol was renamed.
The ISIN stays the same when the symbol changes.

ask.q: When is the next results meeting, and when was it announced?
ask.method: bm_date, intimation_ts, is_results_meeting=1, through the symbol map
ask.plain: A meeting counts as known only after its intimation time.

ask.q: Is a name on a surveillance list today?
ask.plain: Only snapshot days exist, so only those days can be answered.

ask.q: Did the downloader skip a date?
ask.method: status and note for the date
ask.plain: Every date tried has a row with its outcome.

ask.method: first bar in the lake (AsOfView.symbol_info); official date in securities_master
ask.plain: The engine uses the first price bar. The official listing date is in the master list.
Sectors are not in the database. They are in a reference file.

ask.q: What is in the live state?
ask.plain: Once the file exists. It is a separate database from the lake.

ask_note: Run these from the repository folder. mode=ro opens the file read-only, so nothing you type can change it. The pattern passes the SQL as an argument, which keeps single quotes inside the SQL working. The DATA_GUIDE shows the SQL inside the command text, which breaks for queries that contain quotes.

queries.title: Last 5 bars for a symbol (raw prices)
queries.sql: SELECT trade_date, open_raw, high_raw, low_raw, close_raw, volume_raw FROM market_data_lake WHERE symbol='RELIANCE' ORDER BY trade_date DESC LIMIT 5;

queries.title: All actions for a symbol
queries.sql: SELECT ex_date, action_type, ratio_numerator, ratio_denominator, evidence_tier FROM corporate_actions_log WHERE symbol='SBIN' AND action_type <> 'DIVIDEND' ORDER BY ex_date;

queries.title: Sessions in a year (from the Nifty series)
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM market_data_lake WHERE symbol='NIFTY50_INDEX' AND trade_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31';

queries.title: A split in raw prices
queries.sql: SELECT trade_date, close_raw, volume_raw FROM market_data_lake WHERE symbol='SBIN' AND trade_date BETWEEN '2014-11-17' AND '2014-11-24' ORDER BY trade_date;

queries.title: How a renamed symbol is linked
queries.sql: SELECT isin, symbol, first_date, last_date, isin_class, canonical_symbol FROM isin_symbol_map WHERE canonical_symbol='ETERNAL' ORDER BY first_date;
queries.returned: Returned ZOMATO 2021-07-23 to 2025-04-08 and ETERNAL 2025-04-09 to 2026-09-30, both pure_rename, canonical ETERNAL.

glossary.def: Average daily traded value: raw close times raw volume, averaged over recent sessions. Always computed from raw prices and raw volume.
NSE's regular trading series. Only EQ rows were kept in the lake, so a name that moves to another series looks absent.
NSE's label for the trading segment of a security, such as EQ, BE or BZ. Only EQ is in the price tables.
The price exactly as traded that day. The lake stores only raw prices, so a split shows as a jump.
A raw price rescaled for splits and bonuses so history lines up with today. Computed in memory, never stored.
The first session on which a buyer no longer gets the right, for example the split. The action log records only this date.
Point-in-time: using only what was knowable on the day. A number that was known later must not be used earlier.
NSE's end-of-day price file for all securities, published each session.
The newer Bhavcopy file layout used from mid-2024. The downloader handles it and the older layout.
A permanent security identifier. It stays the same when the trading symbol changes.
The short NSE trading code of a security, such as RELIANCE. It can change when a company renames itself.
The latest symbol of a renamed security. The lake stores the whole history under it.
A day on which the exchange traded. The lake's sessions are the dates of the Nifty 50 series.
The date a query pretends to be standing on. Nothing after it can be seen.
The only door from the engine to the lake. It applies the as-of date inside the SQL and raises FutureDataError for a later date.
The error AsOfView raises when asked for a bar dated after the as-of date. There is no way to read the future.
The project's name for finsight.db, the big market-data database.
A holding table where raw downloads land before they are checked and moved on.
The one-time reviewed step that replaced the lake's Yahoo-adjusted rows with raw NSE rows from staging.
NSE sometimes answers a holiday request with the previous session's file. The downloader rejects a file whose own date is not the requested date.
A weekend or holiday on which NSE traded, such as the Diwali evening session.
A company divides each share into several. The price falls by the ratio and the share count rises.
Free extra shares for each share held. The price falls and the share count rises.
A label saying how well the price data confirmed an action: STRONG, WEAK, WEAK_DIRECTIONAL, UNSUPPORTED or NOT_PRICE_MOVING.
A company splits off a part into a new company. The engine does not adjust prices for it.
The moment a company tells the exchange about something, such as a board meeting. A meeting counts as known only after it.
Additional Surveillance Measure: an NSE list of stocks under extra watch, long-term or short-term.
Graded Surveillance Measure: an NSE list that grades stocks under restrictions.
A copy of a list as it stood on one day. NSE gives no history, so snapshots are the only way to keep it.
The append-only history of the live account: init, operator reports and each session's decisions.
Rows may be added but never changed or removed. Triggers refuse any UPDATE or DELETE.
A rule stored inside the database that runs on an event, here to abort an UPDATE or DELETE.
Recomputing the live state by replaying the journal from the first row.
A rule that makes the database enforce a link between tables. This database declares none: its links are logical.
Opened so that nothing can be written. The lake is opened with SQLite mode=ro plus query_only.
Known issue: an entry in the data audit's list of limits, such as KI-001.

triggers.name: trg_tal_no_update
triggers.plain: Aborts any UPDATE with the message append-only.

triggers.name: trg_tal_no_delete
triggers.plain: Aborts any DELETE with the message append-only.
